name: Kettle Creek
worldBackground: Kettle Creek is a small prairie town whose four-block main street still carries the rhythm of daily life: coffee at the diner, nails and advice at the hardware store, long-term residents in the motel's back units. The mood is warm, unhurried and a little tired, with conversation that always circles back to the same topics. The tension is that the new highway bypass routes travelers around town, and every empty parking spot on Main Street is counted as a bad omen.

setting.technology: modern: cars, power grid, mobile phones with spotty signal
setting.climate: temperate plains, hot summers and windy winters

zones.name: Main Street
zones.description: A two-lane paved main street lined with the town's few businesses, angled parking and old streetlights.

buildings.name: Rosie's Diner
buildings.purpose: coffee, breakfast plates and local gossip from open to close

buildings.name: Halvorsen Hardware
buildings.purpose: tools, lumber, paint and repair advice from the owner

buildings.name: Bluebird Motel
buildings.purpose: cheap weekly rooms for travelers and a few long-term tenants

buildings.name: Carter's Garage
buildings.purpose: car and truck repairs for the whole town

zones.name: Maple Row
zones.description: A quiet side street of modest single-family homes with trimmed lawns and picket fences.

buildings.name: Whitaker House
buildings.purpose: family home of the diner's morning cook

buildings.name: Ortiz House
buildings.purpose: home of the schoolteacher and her retired father

buildings.name: Prairie Cottage
buildings.purpose: small home of the elderly hardware store founder

zones.name: Creek Bend Park
zones.description: A grassy strip along the creek with a footbridge, picnic tables and the town water tower standing over it all.

templates.name: Diner booth
templates.description: A bench-table-bench booth where regulars linger over bottomless coffee at Rosie's.
templates.physicalDescription: A rectangular table flanked by two dark green vinyl bench seats, shiny from decades of sliding in.
templates.rule: Rows along the street windows of Rosie's Diner, seats facing the counter, with a clear aisle to the door.

templates.name: Counter stool
templates.description: A chrome-and-vinyl stool that regulars claim by name before sunrise.
templates.physicalDescription: A round red vinyl seat on a chrome pedestal with a small footring, a bright dot from above.
templates.rule: One even row along the customer side of the diner counter, the end stool nearest the register.

templates.name: Diner counter
templates.description: Rosie's counter, where coffee is poured and half the town's news changes hands.
templates.physicalDescription: A long stainless-top counter with napkin dispensers and a register at one end.
templates.rule: One counter dividing Rosie's front room from the kitchen pass; the coffee urn and griddle stay behind it.

templates.name: Coffee urn
templates.description: A big battered urn that never goes cold between five a.m. and closing.
templates.physicalDescription: A squat steel cylinder with a spigot and a stack of white mugs beside it.
templates.rule: Behind the diner counter beside the griddle pass; exactly one, refilled through the morning rush.

templates.name: Flat-top griddle
templates.description: The griddle where the morning cook, when not at home on Maple Row, lays out hash browns at dawn.
templates.physicalDescription: A wide black steel cooktop with a grease-warped shelf of squeeze bottles behind it.
templates.rule: Against the back wall of Rosie's kitchen in the corner, with the coffee urn within arm's reach.

templates.name: Lumber rack
templates.description: Stacked two-by-fours and plywood sheets under a tarp behind Halvorsen's.
templates.physicalDescription: Low wooden A-frame racks with neat stacks of dimensioned lumber, one tarp tied over the top.
templates.rule: In the fenced back yard of Halvorsen Hardware, in rows clear of the fence line and the neighbor's drive.

templates.name: Kitchen table
templates.description: A worn kitchen table where breakfast arguments and supper silence both happen.
templates.physicalDescription: A rectangular table with an oilcloth cover, chairs tucked under its long sides.
templates.rule: Center of every Maple Row kitchen, sized to the household: four chairs at the Whitakers', two at the Prairie Cottage.

templates.name: Kitchen chair
templates.description: A straight-backed wooden chair that has outlived three table tops.
templates.physicalDescription: A simple wooden chair seen from above as a square seat and a back slat.
templates.rule: Two to four around each kitchen table plus one spare beside the couch in the Ortiz parlor; never left in a walkway.

templates.name: Double bed
templates.description: A firm old double bed, the kind the Bluebird rents by the week.
templates.physicalDescription: A rectangular bed with a patchwork or chenille cover, pillow at the head end.
templates.rule: Head against a wall with a dresser alongside; one per sleeper in the Bluebird's back units and one per bedroom on Maple Row.

templates.name: Dresser
templates.description: A scuffed dresser with a lamp on top and, in the motel units, a Bible nobody opens.
templates.physicalDescription: A square wooden chest with a lamp shade visible on top from above.
templates.rule: Beside the foot of every bed, lamp facing it; long-term tenants' dressers sit against the wall nearest their hot plate.

templates.name: Couch
templates.description: A sagging sofa where the motel's long-term tenants watch the evening news.
templates.physicalDescription: A long fabric couch with two crushed cushions and arms worn shiny.
templates.rule: Against the far wall of the Bluebird's back units' sitting corner and the Ortiz parlor; never in the nightly traveler rooms.

templates.name: Hardware shelving
templates.description: Floor-to-ceiling shelving holding nails, paint and every washer size in the county.
templates.physicalDescription: A long narrow aisle of steel shelving with small boxes and gallon paint cans in tidy rows.
templates.rule: Two parallel aisles down the middle of Halvorsen's floor, fasteners nearest the door and paint at the back, a wheelbarrow's width between.

templates.name: Sales counter
templates.description: A counter where Halvorsen writes up orders and motel guests take their key.
templates.physicalDescription: A long wooden counter with a register, a service bell and a stool behind it.
templates.rule: One across the front of Halvorsen Hardware near the door; a second, smaller one inside the Bluebird's office window.

templates.name: Garage workbench
templates.description: Carter's scarred workbench where half the town's engine troubles come to die.
templates.physicalDescription: A long heavy bench with a pegboard of outlined tools above and a vise at one end.
templates.rule: Along the back wall of Carter's Garage, clear of the bay doors' swing.

templates.name: Car lift
templates.description: A hydraulic lift holding somebody's pickup at chest height, hood already up.
templates.physicalDescription: Steel lift posts and arms with a truck undercarriage and open hood above them.
templates.rule: One per bay inside Carter's Garage, hoisted vehicles nose-in toward the right-side yard, never facing Main Street.

templates.name: Tire stack
templates.description: Pyramids of takeoff tires leaning by the garage, priced in chalk.
templates.physicalDescription: A stack of three or four black tires with chalk prices on the sidewalls.
templates.rule: Beside Carter's Garage in its right-hand yard in short pyramids, away from the creek side of town.

templates.name: Streetlight
templates.description: The old Main Street lights that come on one by one at dusk.
templates.physicalDescription: A tall dark pole with a curved arm and teardrop lamp head, a small circle of shadow at its base.
templates.rule: Evenly spaced along both edges of Main Street with one marking the notice board corner; none on Maple Row.

templates.name: Pickup truck
templates.description: A work pickup, usually Halvorsen's or a rancher's, parked where everyone can count it.
templates.physicalDescription: A long cab-and-bed truck with dusty paint, seen from above as a cab box plus open bed.
templates.rule: Nose-in to the curb in Main Street's angled spots or the Bluebird's front lot; every empty painted spot counts as a bad omen.

templates.name: Park bench
templates.description: A slatted bench that has held three generations of waiting spouses.
templates.physicalDescription: A wooden slat bench on iron legs, green paint peeling to gray.
templates.rule: Pairs between streetlights on Main Street and singles facing the creek along the park path.

templates.name: Trash bin
templates.description: A green town bin, emptied behind the diner every evening.
templates.physicalDescription: A round green drum with a domed lid and a tired plastic liner bag showing.
templates.rule: Beside every Main Street bench and the diner's back door, plus one at each park picnic cluster.

templates.name: Notice board
templates.description: The town's wooden bulletin board, half bypass petition and half lost cat.
templates.physicalDescription: A roofed wooden board with layered pinned papers and a pencil stub on a string.
templates.rule: Exactly one, at the center of Main Street beside the diner door, never inside a building.

templates.name: Picnic table
templates.description: A heavy picnic table where supper moves outdoors on the year's hot nights.
templates.physicalDescription: An A-frame table with attached bench seats and initials carved in the planks.
templates.rule: Clusters on the park grass near the footbridge, one grill stand at each cluster's creek side.

templates.name: Grill stand
templates.description: A park grill that still smells of a hundred burgers.
templates.physicalDescription: A short black drum grill on three legs over an ash-dark circle of ground.
templates.rule: One beside each picnic cluster, downwind side toward the creek, never under the water tower's legs.

templates.name: Footbridge
templates.description: The plank footbridge over Kettle Creek, the town's favorite place to stare at water.
templates.physicalDescription: A narrow wooden span with railings on both sides crossing the creek in a straight line.
templates.rule: One span crossing the creek at the park's center, both ends landing on the path; the only crossing in town.

templates.name: Water tower
templates.description: The town water tower, sentinel and compass point over everything.
templates.physicalDescription: Four splayed steel legs rising to a riveted drum with KETTLE CREEK painted in fading white.
templates.rule: One, at the park's far edge behind the picnic ground, visible down the length of Main Street; never beside a building.

templates.name: Picket fence
templates.description: White picket fence, the Maple Row standard, politely climbable in an emergency.
templates.physicalDescription: A line of white pointed pickets with a low rail and gate gaps where lawns meet walks.
templates.rule: Along the front property lines of Maple Row with gaps at every walkway and driveway; never across the back of a lot.

templates.name: Mailbox
templates.description: A curbside mailbox, flag up on pension day.
templates.physicalDescription: A small metal box on a post with a red flag and a house number stenciled on the side.
templates.rule: One per Maple Row house at its walkway, on the street side of the picket fence, never inside the fence line itself.

templates.name: Shade tree
templates.description: An old cottonwood or maple that every yard on the row is quietly proud of.
templates.physicalDescription: A broad canopy from above, a wide green disc with dappled shadow at its edge.
templates.rule: One mature tree per Maple Row front lawn set off-center from the house, plus scattered cottonwoods along the creek bank.

templates.name: Driveway
templates.description: A concrete strip from back door to street, oil-stained where the truck drips.
templates.physicalDescription: A pale concrete strip with hairline cracks and dark drip stains, meeting the curb at the street.
templates.rule: One strip per Maple Row house from its door to the street through the picket gap, a pickup parked on it.

templates.name: Prairie grass tuft
templates.description: Tough prairie grass and wildflowers anywhere the mower gives up.
templates.physicalDescription: A clump of mixed grass with stubby wildflowers and pale seed heads, bare dirt at the edges.
templates.rule: Scatter on the park's unmown edges, vacant corners and roadside verges; never on pavement, trimmed lawns or in fence gaps.

npcs.name: Dale Whitaker
npcs.description: The diner's morning cook, who wants the counter stools full again by six and worries the bypass has cut his breakfast trucks from a dozen down to three.
npcs.physicalDescription: Heavyset, in a bleach-spotted apron over flannel, with a crescent-shaped burn scar on his left forearm.

npcs.name: Astrid Halvorsen
npcs.role: founder and owner of Halvorsen Hardware
npcs.description: The eighty-one-year-old founder of the hardware store, who still opens six days a week because she wants to hand the keys to someone before her knees quit first.
npcs.physicalDescription: Tiny and straight-backed, in a man's wool vest and orthopedic shoes, clicking her ring of a hundred cut keys like a metronome.

npcs.name: Marisol Ortiz
npcs.description: Teacher of the county's smallest class, nine students this year, who wants a tenth desk filled by spring and fears the bypass will empty the schoolhouse for good.
npcs.physicalDescription: Compact and quick-moving, in corduroys and a hand-knit scarf, a red grading pen parked behind her ear at all hours.

npcs.name: Ernesto Ortiz
npcs.role: retired; volunteer caretaker of the park
npcs.description: Marisol's retired father, who sweeps the footbridge and the six picnic tables every morning because he wants the town to look lived-in and worries he'll be the last one left to do it.
npcs.physicalDescription: Gaunt, in a canvas work jacket and feed cap, fingers stained dark from shelling walnuts on the bench.

npcs.name: Rosie Vance
npcs.description: The diner's namesake, who sold her house to keep all four coffee pots hot past supper and counts every empty parking spot on Main Street from the kitchen window.
npcs.physicalDescription: Broad-shouldered with a gravel voice, in jeans and a name-tagged work shirt, a pencil worn to a stub behind her ear.

npcs.name: Gus Bell
npcs.description: The motel's owner-manager, who wants his fourteen weekly rooms full like the old highway days and worries about the flicker in the vacancy sign he can't trace to any wire.
npcs.physicalDescription: Lean and sun-creased, in a pearl-snap western shirt, with keys on a carabiner that jingle before you see him coming.

npcs.name: Jesse Carter
npcs.description: The town's only mechanic, who rented a motel back room after his divorce and wants the county plow contract to carry the shop through winter, worried the bypass sends breakdowns to a rival garage thirty miles east.
npcs.physicalDescription: Barrel-chested, in gray coveralls with his name faded off the chest, a white scar splitting one eyebrow.

player.name: Dana Mercer
player.description: An outsider hired by the county to spend the winter counting cars and empty parking spots for a bypass impact report, who wants her numbers to be honest and worries they'll be the last thing that finishes this town off.
player.physicalDescription: Tall and windburned, in a fleece-lined surveyor's vest and insulated boots, clicking a metal tally counter without noticing she's doing it.
